headline: Workflows for haplotype-resolved assembly, sex chromosomes and variant calling
label: Genome Assembly And Variant Calling
summary: Recent preprints benchmark assembly and phasing workflows for non-model and hybrid genomes, alongside a consensus variant caller.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the construction of reliable, structurally resolved genomes from difficult inputs: low-coverage pooled reads, ethanol-preserved specimens, hybrid diploids and long-read data. Several items benchmark workflows directly, including Nanopore assembly of Dermacentor reticulatus with attention to error correction, coverage limits and synteny-based chromosome assignment, and a comparison of local PCA, SyRI alignment and pangenome graphs for Timema inversions. Other items target specific architectures: CBS-tools uses sex-specific k-mer quantification to identify the heterogametic sex and phase sex chromosomes, and HipHap assigns reads to haplotypes with a HapQ confidence score. ChoCallate combines bcftools, FreeBayes and GATK for consensus germline calling, tested on simulated Arabidopsis and 200 wheat samples. What distinguishes these items is their emphasis on haplotype-aware, reproducible pipelines rather than single-method assemblies.
